state_meaning: AI-drafted candidate; no person has reviewed it.
text: On 438 binary comparison questions about helpfulness, honesty and harmlessness, the paper compares a preference model trained on human feedback with pretrained language models answering the comparisons as multiple-choice questions, and reports that chain-of-thought reasoning significantly improves performance; the authors state the trends suggest models larger than 52B will be competitive with human-feedback-trained preference models.
title: LM judges of helpful/honest/harmless comparisons approach human-feedback preference models
